title: CQC care-home deregistration within 12 months
summary: Research task: at the production instant of a monthly CQC 'HSCA Active Locations' register vintage T (England), predict whether a care-home location's registration ends within the following 12 months - a register event (Location Status Inactive-Dereg or Removed with a Location HSCA End Date in (T, T+365d], joined from the cumulative Deactivated Locations product) - using only that vintage's own published columns: beds, service types and user bands, latest overall rating and its recency, HSCA start year, geography and provider sector. One row per active care home at a January vintage, 107,652 rows across fixed temporal splits on the vintage instant (train 78,138 over January vintages 2018-2022, eval 14,765 at 2024-01-05, holdout 14,749 at 2025-01-02). A retrospective, mixed-vintage construction over per-file-sha256-pinned CQC open-data extracts - not an operational screening tool and not a point-in-time reconstruction.
domain: adult social care regulation / register-exit prediction

post.title: Will a care home leave the CQC register within a year? Vintage-time features, register events only
paragraphs: The Care Quality Commission publishes its register as open data (Open Government Licence v3.0): monthly 'HSCA Active Locations' snapshots with a public archive of 2011-2026 vintages, plus a cumulative 'Deactivated Locations' file. The contribution here is not access: it is the per-file-sha256-pinned source extracts, the derived register-event label, the care-home eligibility frame with counted exclusions (the 2016 and 2017 vintages are dropped loudly for unresolved required columns; the 2023 vintage is excluded by design so every train target window closes at least 12 months before the eval instant), fixed disjoint temporal splits on the vintage instant, and a scored, reproducible contract. 107,652 rows: train 78,138 across the January vintages 2018-2022 (4,418 positives, 5.65%), eval 14,765 at the 2024-01-05 vintage (757, 5.13%), and a labelled holdout 14,749 at 2025-01-02 (761, 5.16%) that ships but is never scored in development.

The packaged baseline is illustrative, and the comparisons decide what the number means. The stock runner-contract baseline reaches eval AUC 0.5659 on the 14,765 eval rows; on identical rows the simple rate references reach: rating-x-beds bucket 0.5871 (the strongest; paired bootstrap difference over the last-rating rate +0.0273, 95% CI [0.0123, 0.0407], excludes zero), last-rating 0.5597, beds bucket 0.5298, HSCA start-year 0.5226, local authority 0.5207, provider sector 0.5011, with majority-class accuracy 0.9487 on this split. The model beats every one-line prior yet trails the strongest rate reference: recorded as a defect of the stock runner under this protocol, not a no-headroom verdict - a verified diagnosis candidate sits beside it (the stock runner treats the vintage instant as a train-only categorical, so the eval instant is unseen), and no universal claim is made in either direction. There is no persistence reference by design: identity ships as a per-instant pseudonym, so prior-instant labels are structurally unlinkable - for any scorer.

Honest framing, measured rather than asserted. The prediction instant is the vintage's production date (the publisher's own file-stamping convention) and every shipped feature is that vintage's own column; the measured as-of check found 0 of the 14,765 eval rows carrying a rating publication date after the instant. The target is the register event - deregistration of the location - which CQC's own in-file note says can include a service continuing under a new registration: BMJ Public Health 2024 evidence implies roughly 40-55% of register events are re-registrations or transfers rather than complete closures. The label source (Deactivated Locations) never ships as a feature, and instants whose 12-month target window extends past the deactivated file's coverage are excluded as unobserved.

The construction is retrospective and mixed-vintage (historical Active-Locations vintages plus the current cumulative deactivated register): there is no full-row availability ledger, training-label timing is unverified, and the evaluation contract is retrospective research requiring isolated rows - one row per solver context. Cross-row outcome exposure is declared and measured, not enforced: pseudonym-successor probes cover 0 rows in every split, and the quasi-identifier (local authority x beds x start year x rating x sector) covers 0 rows across the eval/holdout boundary (11,786 rows within train, where labels are public by design anyway). The labelled holdout is downloadable by design and stays outside every evaluated agent's workspace. Publication is gated on an independent adversarial pre-flip audit of the frozen package, per the standing practice since 2026-10-27.

limitations: Derived research dataset, not an official Care Quality Commission product; CQC has not reviewed, authorised or endorsed it. The publisher's data is Open Government Licence v3.0 (attribution 'Care Quality Commission' required); our compilation contribution is dedicated CC0-1.0 and the code is MIT. CQC's in-sheet disclaimer is carried: CQC is not responsible for subsequent analysis, and the dataset must not be quoted as its source.

The target is a REGISTER EVENT, not a service closure: CQC's in-file note says deregistration can include a service continuing under a new registration, and BMJ Public Health 2024 implies roughly 40-55% of register events are re-registrations or transfers rather than complete closures.

Retrospective, mixed-vintage construction (historical Active-Locations vintages plus the current cumulative Deactivated Locations edition): no full-row availability ledger exists, training-label timing is unverified, and no point-in-time reconstruction is claimed.

The evaluation contract is retrospective research requiring isolated rows; the shipped illustrative runner does not enforce that requirement, and scores under unrestricted table access would overstate honest performance.

Cross-row outcome exposure is measured, not enforced: pseudonym-successor probe coverage is 0/0/0 across train/eval/holdout, and quasi-identifier (local authority x beds x start year x rating x sector) coverage is 0 across the eval/holdout boundary (11,786 rows within train, where labels are public by design).
Identity ships as a per-instant salted pseudonym (the missing-successor design): prior-instant labels are structurally unlinkable, so no persistence reference exists - by design, and for any scorer.
The 2016 and 2017 vintages are dropped loudly (unresolved required columns) and the 2023 vintage is excluded by design so every train target window closes at least 12 months before the eval instant.

The stock runner baseline (eval AUC 0.5659) is quoted only beside its references (strongest rate reference 0.5871 with a paired bootstrap interval excluding zero, last-rating 0.5597, beds 0.5298, start-year 0.5226, local authority 0.5207, provider sector 0.5011; majority-class accuracy 0.9487 on this split); the number is never quoted alone, and the recorded runner defect (unseen eval instant) sits beside it.
The labelled holdout is downloadable by design; keep it and its labels outside every evaluated agent's workspace until a design is frozen.
